lean.statement:
∀
  {E : Type u_1} [inst : NormedAddCommGroup E] [inst_1 : InnerProductSpace ℝ E] [inst_2 : FiniteDimensional ℝ E]
  [inst_3 : MeasurableSpace E] [inst_4 : BorelSpace E] (W f : E → ℝ),
  ContDiff ℝ 2 W →
    ContDiff ℝ (↑⊤) f →
      HasCompactSupport f →
        have L := fun x => Laplacian.laplacian f x - Inner.inner ℝ (gradient W x) (gradient f x);
        have H := fun x => ∑ i, ‖gradient (fun z => (fderiv ℝ f z) ((stdOrthonormalBasis ℝ E) i)) x‖ ^ 2;
        have C := fun x => ((fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ W) x) (gradient f x)) (gradient f x);
        MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x) * L x ^ 2) MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume ∧
          MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x) * ‖gradient f x‖ ^ 2) MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume ∧
            MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x) * H x) MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume ∧
              MeasureTheory.Integrable (fun x => Real.exp (-W x) * C x) MeasureTheory.MeasureSpace.volume ∧
                ∫ (x : E), Real.exp (-W x) * L x ^ 2 =
                    (∫ (x : E), Real.exp (-W x) * H x) + ∫ (x : E), Real.exp (-W x) * C x ∧
                  ∀ (m : ℝ),
                    (∀ (x v : E), m * ‖v‖ ^ 2 ≤ ((fderiv ℝ (fderiv ℝ W) x) v) v) →
                      m * ∫ (x : E), Real.exp (-W x) * ‖gradient f x‖ ^ 2 ≤ ∫ (x : E), Real.exp (-W x) * L x ^ 2
approved_definition_context: The ambient type is a finite-dimensional real inner-product space with Borel measurable structure. The default measure in a real integral is canonical volume.

ContDiff at order 2 is C2 and at order infinity is smooth. HasCompactSupport means the closure of the nonzero support is compact. fderiv is the genuine Frechet derivative; gradient is its Riesz representative; Laplacian is the canonical trace of the genuine second derivative.

stdOrthonormalBasis is an orthonormal basis indexed by Fin(finrank R E), empty in dimension zero. The displayed sum of squared gradients of directional derivatives is explicit; no abstract Hessian norm equality is an additional premise.
Integrable means almost-everywhere strong measurability and finite integral of the norm; signed curvature terms require actual integrability. Lets name displayed expressions, not hypotheses.

Measure.map is pushforward and Measure.prod is independent product. stdGaussian is the standard Gaussian. Tilted is normalized exponential weighting, totalized to zero if the exponential weight is not integrable.
A Markov kernel is a measurably parameterized probability measure. IsCondKernel disintegrates the specified joint measure conditional on its first coordinate; Prod.swap exchanges coordinates.
